minutes.headline: Design committee favored a hybrid plan keeping Town Hall as a meeting house; no vote except adjournment.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed three building concepts and a chair-built hybrid for Town Hall, Ritter, TC Passios, Brooks House and 30 School Street. Members leaned toward the hybrid, debated whether meeting-room use justifies renovating Town Hall, and planned the joint Select Board meeting. Storage replies from the schools and Town Manager were reviewed, and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

Closing public comment: none substantive, only light remarks about Town Hall.

what_happened.line: The Municipal Building Design Committee took no votes; members leaned toward a chair-built hybrid plan that keeps Town Hall as a meeting house.
The committee agreed to present the hybrid option for discussion at next week's joint meeting with the Select Board.
The committee will offer to meet with the School Committee, Planning Board and Finance Committee; the chair will reach out to representatives.
The chair argued that paying someone to digitize records for two years would cost less than building a records storage room.
Replies on storage needs from the superintendent's office and the Town Manager were reviewed, and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

why_it_matters: The hybrid would decide whether Town Hall is renovated and kept in use, which affects how much new building space the town may later be asked to pay for and vote on.
The records question, digitizing versus a storage room, is a cost trade-off that could change the size of any building project put before residents.
